title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
abstract: arXiv:2610.32411v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. Prior studies attribute this capability to retrieval heads, a sparse set of attention heads that transfer information from the context to the output. However, these analyses are confined to a limited set of modalities and the corresponding models. Moreover, how retrieval heads can be leveraged to enhance the model calls for further exploration. In this paper, we ask whether this mechanism expands together with the input modalities of the model. Taking audio-visual input as a newly added modality, we construct paired inputs in which the same answer is either spoken or shown on screen. With the evidence content fixed, retrieval heads remain sparse in the new modality and are shared to a large extent across modalities. translated_title: 更广泛地审视多模态大语言模型的检索头
translated_abstract: 在长输入中定位相关证据是多模态大语言模型（MLLM）的一项核心能力。先前的研究将这种能力归因于检索头（retrieval heads），即一组稀疏的注意力头，负责将信息从上下文传递到输出。然而，这些分析仅局限于有限的模态集合及相应的模型。此外，如何利用检索头来增强模型仍有待进一步探索。本文探究了这一机制是否会随模型输入模态的扩展而扩展。我们将视听输入作为一种新增模态，构建了成对输入，其中相同的答案既通过语音说出，也在屏幕上显示。在证据内容保持固定的情况下，检索头在新模态中依然保持稀疏，并在很大程度上跨模态共享。在18个语言、视觉-语言和全模态模型检查点上，全模态模型在很大程度上保留了原有模态的检索头。
tldr: 该研究通过构建语音与画面内容相同的视听配对输入发现，检索头机制随新增模态依然保持稀疏并在跨模态间高度共享，且全模态模型在很大程度上保留了原有模态的检索头。
en_tdlr: By constructing paired inputs where the same evidence is either spoken or shown on screen, this study shows that retrieval heads remain sparse and largely shared across modalities when audio-visual input is added, and omni-modal models largely preserve the retrieval heads of their earlier modality-specific counterparts.
